group: Valid – exactly one subschema matches

cases.expected: empty Set (no ValidationMessage), because only one subschema validates
cases.description: The JSON instance matches exactly one of the 'oneOf' subschemas, so validation should succeed with no errors.

group: Invalid – no subschema matches

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage with message containing 'oneOf' and 'must match exactly one schema'
cases.description: The JSON instance does not satisfy any of the subschemas, therefore OneOfValidator must return a validation error.

group: Invalid – more than one subschema matches

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage indicating that more than one schema matched
cases.description: The instance satisfies two subschemas, violating the 'oneOf' rule; validator must report an error.

group: Edge – node is null

cases.expected: empty Set (validation passes) if schema allows null, otherwise a ValidationMessage about type mismatch
cases.description: When the instance node is null, OneOfValidator should either succeed (if null is permitted by any subschema) or fail; this case expects the subschemas to allow null, resulting in no errors.

group: Edge – schema contains no subschemas (empty oneOf)

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage stating that 'oneOf' must contain at least one schema
cases.description: If the OneOfValidator is constructed with an empty list of subschemas, validation should fail immediately with a clear error.

group: Short‑circuit enabled – first matching subschema stops further checks

cases.expected: empty Set, and verification that only the first matching subschema’s validate method was invoked
cases.description: When canShortCircuit() is true, OneOfValidator should stop evaluating remaining subschemas after the first successful validation, resulting in no errors.

group: Report child errors – false (errors from child validators are suppressed)

cases.expected: Set containing a single ValidationMessage for the oneOf rule, without propagating child schema messages
cases.description: If reportChildErrors() is false, validation should return only the top‑level oneOf error even when child validators produce multiple messages.

group: Walk flag true – validator invoked via walk method

cases.expected: empty Set, same as validate() result, confirming walk delegates correctly
cases.description: Calling walk with shouldValidateSchema=true should produce the same result as validate(), ensuring the delegation logic works.

group: Valid – oneOf with a single subschema

cases.expected: empty Set (no ValidationMessage), because the sole subschema validates successfully
cases.description: When a oneOf array contains exactly one schema, the validator should behave like that schema. The instance satisfies the subschema, so validation succeeds.

group: Invalid – multiple subschemas match and canShortCircuit is false

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage indicating that more than one schema matched (oneOf violation)
cases.description: With short‑circuiting disabled the validator must evaluate all subschemas. The instance satisfies two of them, so a oneOf error should be reported.

group: Valid – multiple subschemas match but canShortCircuit is true (short‑circuit semantics)

cases.expected: empty Set (no ValidationMessage), because validation stops after the first successful subschema
cases.description: When short‑circuiting is enabled the validator stops after the first matching subschema, even if later subschemas would also match. The expected behaviour is a successful validation.

group: Report child errors – true (default) aggregates messages from failing subschemas

cases.expected: Set containing at least two ValidationMessages: one for the oneOf rule and one (or more) from the child schema(s) reporting the 'minimum' violation on 'age'
cases.description: When child errors are reported, the validator should return the top‑level oneOf message plus any messages produced by the subschemas that were evaluated and failed.

group: Valid – array instance matches exactly one subschema

cases.expected: empty Set (no ValidationMessage)
cases.description: The oneOf contains two array‑type subschemas: one requiring exactly three items, another requiring a minimum of five items. The instance matches only the first, so validation succeeds.

group: Invalid – $ref subschema resolves and causes multiple matches

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage indicating that more than one schema matched (oneOf violation)
cases.description: One subschema is a $ref to a definition that validates the object, and another subschema independently validates the same structure. Both match, so a oneOf error must be reported.

group: Valid – oneOf with non‑object schema (type string)

cases.expected: empty Set (no ValidationMessage), because the string matches exactly one of the subschemas (type: string, maxLength: 10)
cases.description: The oneOf array contains a string schema with maxLength 10 and a number schema. The instance is a valid string within the length limit, so only one subschema matches.

group: Invalid – duplicate identical subschemas cause multiple matches

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage stating that more than one schema matched (oneOf violation)
cases.description: The oneOf list contains two identical schemas that both accept the instance. Even though they are duplicates, the validator must detect that more than one schema matches and report an error.

group: Exception – null executionContext

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: validate() dereferences executionContext (e.g., to obtain the schema factory). Passing a null executionContext should cause a NullPointerException.

group: Exception – null instanceLocation

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: The validator builds ValidationMessage objects using the instanceLocation. Supplying a null instanceLocation should trigger a NullPointerException.

group: Exception – null rootNode with non‑null node

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: During $ref resolution the validator may need the root node. Providing a null rootNode while the instance node is non‑null should cause a NullPointerException.

group: Exception – validator constructed with null subschemas list

input.value: mockExecutionContext (validator built with null subschemas list)

cases.expected: IllegalStateException
cases.description: OneOfValidator expects a non‑null collection of subschemas. Supplying a null list at construction time should cause an IllegalStateException when validate() is invoked.

group: Exception – validator contains null subschema entry

input.value: mockExecutionContext (oneOf list contains a null element)

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When iterating over the subschemas, a null entry should cause a NullPointerException because the validator attempts to invoke validate() on it.

group: Exception – oneOf contains non‑schema element

input.value: mockExecutionContext (oneOf array includes a plain string instead of a JsonSchema object)

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: The validator expects each element of the oneOf array to be a JsonSchema. Supplying a non‑schema element (e.g., a raw string) should raise an IllegalArgumentException during validation setup.

group: Exception – circular $ref leads to SchemaException

cases.expected: SchemaException
cases.description: A circular $ref resolution should be detected and reported as a SchemaException (or a subclass) rather than causing infinite recursion or a StackOverflowError.

group: Exception – executionContext with null validatorFactory

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: During validation the ExecutionContext is used to obtain a JsonSchemaFactory. If the factory field is null, a NullPointerException should be thrown.
